subject: Unit economics deep dive & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep dive & next steps

Hi Jamie / Zara —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and really appreciate the transparency on volumes and use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: in-product intelligent summaries + next-action suggestions for customer support tickets (high-frequency, short outputs).
- Expected request profile: 1.2M user-facing requests/month (avg. payload 350 tokens in, 100 tokens out).
- Peak concurrency expected: ~300 rps for the summarization route (short SLOs).

Open questions we promised to follow up on
- Target unit economics: you mentioned aiming for cost <= $800/1M tokens for inference (net infrastructure cost to product).
- CAC / payback targets: expected payback window ~3–6 months for the new feature cohort.
- Additional features: prioritized roadmap (summaries -> triage automation -> proactive suggestions).

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll share a conservative unit-econ model (tokens, latency tiers, cost per 1M tokens, expected margin by feature). Attachment: FintechX_unit-econ-model.xlsx
2) Aditya will do a short runbook with recommended configuration (batching, quantization, routing) and an estimated $/1M tokens under Ded & Hosted options.
3) Marcus to prepare a pricing/commitment proposal (3, 6, 12 month tiers) and potential introductory credit for pilot.

Can we target a follow-up call next Thurs (7/16) to walk the model and align on pilot sizing? If that works, Jamie — please confirm preferred time.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Quick clarifications: 
- The 1.2M requests/month is our internal estimate for the support-summaries feature only; if the pilot expands to triage automation we could see ~2.5x volume.
- The $800/1M tokens is a product-target number (we want inference spend to be <5% of incremental ARR for the feature).
- Payback: product leadership is comfortable with a 4 month CAC payback window if unit economics meet target.

Thu 7/16 works — morning PT is best (9–11am). Please set up a calendar invite and we’ll be ready to go through the workbook.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unit economics deep dive & next steps

Jamie — thanks for the clarity. I ran a quick set of conservative configs based on your profile and attached a short note to the workbook (see FintechX_unit-econ-model.xlsx). Key callouts: 

- Baseline assumptions we used:
  • Input tokens/request: 350 (avg)
  • Output tokens/request: 100 (avg)
  • Effective tokens/request: 450
  • Monthly requests (pilot): 1.2M -> monthly tokens = 540M tokens

- Estimated inference cost (hosted, optimized batching + 8-bit quant)
  • Avg $/1M tokens: $1,200 (baseline; single-model, no long-context optimizations)
  • Optimized $/1M tokens: $700 (with heavy batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variant)

- Recommendation: Pilot with a dedicated pool if you need consistent latency + lower $/1M. With a 6–12 month commit we can hit ~$550–$650/1M tokens depending on load shaping and cache hit rates.

Action items for our call:
- Walk through the workbook and assumptions (Marissa)
- Marcus to present commitment/credit options
- Jamie to confirm pilot scope (summaries-only vs summaries + triage)

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lopez <jamie.lopez@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unit economics deep dive & next steps

Hi all — attaching Redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf with the tiered commitment options I mentioned on the call. Quick summary: 

- Pilot (30 days, no commit): $0.00 setup + usage at hosted pricing (estimated $1,000–$1,300/1M tokens for your profile).
- Trial Reserve (3 months, partial commit): 150k USD reserve -> effective $/1M tokens ~ $750–$900 depending on utilization.
- Standard Commit (6–12 months): $/1M tokens in the $550–$700 range for the volumes you shared.

Notes on margin & CAC framing (to help your finance/product teams):
- If your target is inference cost <= $800/1M tokens and you can achieve a 30% gross margin on the feature at launch, that aligns to a payback window under 6 months for an average ARPU increase of $6–8 per enabled user (back-of-envelope).
- If you expand to triage automation and volumes increase 2.5x, your effective $/1M tokens will trend downward with a reserved pool, improving margin conversion.

Next: Marissa will walk the workbook on Thu 7/16 at 9:30am PT. Marcus will present pricing tiers and a recommended pilot reserve.

—Marcus

Thanks team — the model you shared looks reasonable. A couple quick asks before the call: 
- Can you include a row in the workbook that shows $/feature (i.e., inference cost per enabled user per month) for summaries vs triage? That will help our PMs translate to ARPU lift targets.
- Also include a sensitivity table for cache hit rates (10/30/50%) — we want to understand how much engineering effort on caching moves the needle.

We’re leaning toward a 3-month trial reserve to start (to validate impact) but will make a decision after the walkthrough. Looking forward to Thurs 9:30am PT.

Best,
